findings.title: Section 3's commit gate (3.7) cannot pass — `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` goes red in 3.3 but is only deleted in 4.1
findings.description: Task 3.3 removes the adoption hook from `ContextIntegrator`/`CoreServiceFactory` and names exactly four test files to update (`ContextIntegrator.test.ts`, `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts`, `pipeline-integration.test.ts`, `pure-build-golden.test.ts`). It does not mention `packages/core/tests/adoption/adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts`, which calls the two-argument `createContextPipeline(dir, { adoptionStateWrites, squadronProbe })` (`packages/core/tests/adoption/adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts:68`) and asserts the behavior the slice removes: the brownfield prompt swap (`:100-101`), the `### Adoption Facts` heading (`:102`), and `readAdoptionState(root)` being `'in_progress'` after a build (`:123`, `:209`). As soon as 3.3 lands, these cases fail. Task 3.7 then requires `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm -r test` to **all pass** before committing `refactor: remove adoption hook from the build pipeline`, but the full-suite run must fail on this file — its deletion is only listed at task 4.1 (`:144`), after the 3.7 commit marker. The commit marker therefore sits at a point that is not tested-green, contradicting the file's own success criterion and the "test-with" sequencing the rest of the plan follows (the file's section-4 header even promises "Each task leaves the workspace compiling and commits on its own", but the red window 3.7 → 4.1 crosses a commit). Fix: delete (or rewrite against the kept detection functions, per the design's Migration Plan note) `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` as part of 3.3's test updates, or move 4.1's deletion of that file ahead of the 3.7 commit.
